naklecha reports autonomous kernel-optimization experiments

Naklecha reports that one prompt launched a 16-hour autonomous kernel-optimization run using Cloudy’s autoresearch harness, conducting roughly 150 H200 experiments. They claim ninth place on Meta’s kernel leaderboard, kernels 1.57× faster than SGLang’s, and $250 in token and compute costs.

Xiaoyin Chen evaluates self-evolving agents under task drift

Xiaoyin Chen and coauthors evaluate three self-evolving agent methods across four changing task streams. They report that adaptation often improves aggregate performance but can disrupt earlier or unseen tasks, while memory retrieval remains vulnerable to conflicting workflows.

Vision-Language-Action or World-Action? Just Action Models

JAM trains action policies to predict representations of recorded future observations through a temporary supervision branch. This allows predictive learning across generative, self-supervised and vision-language backbones while retaining ordinary action inference.

ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning

ThinkWorld learns a shared motion-token representation across human and robot experience. Predicted consequences provide reinforcement signals that improve the representations used for robot control and transfer to unfamiliar configurations.

Sagnik Ghosh details Agentic Scientist's research orchestration

Sagnik Ghosh describes Sakana’s Agentic Scientist as an open-source system that coordinates coding agents to propose experiments, measure results, run ablations and produce papers with claim-level evidence checks. He highlights the authors’ reported finding that model choice mattered more than harness choice across 70 test campaigns, alongside limitations involving computational ML tasks and reward hacking.

RubricAtlas: Mining Type-Level Rubrics from Expert Reports to Evaluate Deep Research Agents

RubricAtlas derives reusable analytical requirements from multiple expert reports within a research type. It evaluates which analyses agents complete while keeping argument validity separate.

XSocial postOct 27, 2026

Paul Iusztin outlines CodeClimb's evaluation-driven experiment loop

Paul Iusztin describes CodeClimb, an agent system he is building to improve code through repeated experiments. Its proposed workflow generates three sandboxed candidates, scores them with separate evaluators, uses feedback to continue searching, and reserves test data for final evaluation. He identifies GraphRAG as the initial application and promotes Inngest as the infrastructure supporting long-running experiments.

arXivPaperOct 27, 2026

MLE-World: Predicting Machine Learning Experiment Outcomes with a Learned World Model

MLE-World predicts the feedback an ML experiment would produce without running it. Research agents use predicted logs, errors and validation scores to explore more candidate programs, while confidence gating determines when to obtain real feedback.
